strategy.title: No plan inside 21 days: the signed permit-packet deals settle net-45
strategy.why: The only opening has four written acceptances at $2,000 each ($8,000, enough for the $5,000 target, cost $30 and no capital), but its evidenced payment terms are net-45 from invoice, so no cash settles inside the 21-day window.

alternatives.why: Brings $8,000 but after the deadline; counts only if the owner moves the deadline to at least 45 days.

alternatives.why: Would change the settlement link, but no record shows any buyer accepting earlier terms; it is a question to measure, not evidence.

brain.summary: INFEASIBLE AS STATED: inside the goal's own limits the openings held bring at most $0 of the $5,000 still needed, even with every buyer agreeing at the top price. To make it supportable, deadline: move the deadline to at least 45 days from now, when enough lots have settled; or target: lower the target: the openings held bring nothing inside the goal's limits even with every buyer agreeing. The conclusion covers the openings held; markets nobody has counted are not ruled out, so Brain keeps searching for openings outside them.

reviews.reasons: NO_PLAN is correct and the decisive gap is the one the evidence decides: four written acceptances at $2,000 ($8,000, which would cover $5,000 at $30 cost and no capital) are payable net-45 from invoice, and the card's timeToFirstCash is 45 days against a 21-day window. That is a real constraint - even with every link held as evidenced, nothing settles in the window - not missing evidence. Brain's own check agrees (at most $0 inside the limits). The alternatives (move the deadline to >=45 days, or obtain a written earlier-payment term) are the right two, and the plan correctly refuses to treat a hoped-for deposit as evidence.
findings: Recomputed: 4 x $2,000 = $8,000 >= $5,000; cost $30 << price; capital $0 <= $500 cap; but settlement day 45 > 21, so in-window cash is $0.
The constraint is cited to the card's own timeToFirstCash and price facts (net-45), not an assumption.

Possible avenue not considered: invoice factoring/early-payment financing within the $500 capital cap - unevidenced, so not a reason to revise, but worth a research question if the owner keeps the 21-day deadline.
Acceptances are recorded by a PERSON as written acceptances; no contradicting record.
